title: Refresh an expiring SDDC Manager token mid-rotation without losing work
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Our ESXi SSH passwords are past their rotation window, and last night's maintenance job died part way through when its API token expired: some hosts were rotated, some were not, and the job then re-ran rotations it had already completed. Rebuild it properly.

Implement `VcfCredentialRotation.psm1` at the workspace root. It must rotate the SSH password of every ESXi host SDDC Manager knows about and survive the access token expiring in the middle of the run.

The runner installs `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` 13.5.0.25380678 and its dependencies. Import that genuine PowerCLI SDK module and build every request body with its model initializers, including `Initialize-VcfTokenCreationSpec`, `Initialize-VcfBaseCredential`, `Initialize-VcfResourceCredentials`, and `Initialize-VcfCredentialsUpdateSpec`. Do not vendor VMware modules into the repository.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification rather than a documentation page, and it is pinned to the `9.0.0.0` tag, not the `9.1.0.0` revision of the same file. The only operationIds in scope are `createToken`, `refreshAccessToken`, `getCredentials`, `updateOrRotatePasswords`, and `getCredentialsTask`; nothing else is served.

The acceptance harness calls:

`Invoke-VcfCredentialRotation -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -ResourceType <string> -CredentialType <string> [-PageSize <int>] [-MaxPolls <int>] [-SleepAction <scriptblock>]`

Requirements:

- Export only `Invoke-VcfCredentialRotation`. `-Server` is the appliance base URL. `PageSize` defaults to 2 and `MaxPolls` to 30. When `SleepAction` is supplied, invoke it with the delay in seconds instead of calling `Start-Sleep`, and never wait after a terminal poll or after the final permitted poll.
- Sign in once with `createToken`, keeping both the returned `accessToken` and the `refreshToken.id`.
- Page through `getCredentials` filtered to the requested resource type, using `pageNumber` and `pageSize`, until every page has been read. Leave `resourceName`, `resourceIp`, `domainName`, and `accountType` unset: an unset optional query parameter must be absent from the query string, never sent as an empty value.
- Rotate only the credentials whose `credentialType` matches the requested one, with one `updateOrRotatePasswords` call per host. Send `operationType` `ROTATE` and one `ResourceCredentials` element carrying that host's `resourceId`, its `resourceType`, and its `BaseCredential` entries. A rotation asks SDDC Manager to generate the new secret, so `password` must be absent from every credential; `autoRotatePolicy` is unset and must be absent as well.
- Each accepted rotation returns `202` with a task. Poll `getCredentialsTask` until it reports a terminal state, treating `SUCCESSFUL` as success and `FAILED`, `USER_CANCELLED`, and `INCONSISTENT` as failure.
- The access token expires part way through the run. When SDDC Manager answers `401`, exchange the refresh token id for a new access token with `refreshAccessToken`, then replay the rejected request with the new token and carry on. `refreshAccessToken` is a `PATCH` whose body is a bare JSON string holding the refresh token id: it is not an object and must not be double-encoded. Do not authenticate again — `createToken` must be called exactly once for the whole run — and no host may be rotated twice or skipped because of the expiry.
- Return an object exposing `ResourceIds`, `TaskIds`, and `TokenRefreshed`.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It starts contract-pinned loopback SDDC Manager fixtures on `127.0.0.1`, drives the module with dummy credentials, and reads their request logs to check the exact method, target, query string, body member set, bearer token discipline, polling behavior, and the omission of every unset optional field. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_sddc.py`, `.gitignore`, and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
